prerequisites: Contents of the first semester, especially Programming 1

learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the concepts of the most common algorithms and data structures.
Students have the ability to create high-quality programs using algorithms and data structures.
Students can implement their own algorithms and data structures and defend them against competing approaches.
As part of the course, programming exercises take place. Students are therefore also able to understand, criticize, and complement algorithms and data structures of other students.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Algorithm definition, classification of algorithms
Graphs: Graph definitions, applications in computer science, Shortest Path, Lowest Cost, A*
Complexity analysis: Time complexity, O-, Omega-, and Theta-calculus, Space complexity
Lists: Arrays, dynamic arrays/lists, amortization, basic operations, stacks, queues, linked lists
Recursion: Search, Divide and Conquer, recurrence relations, backtracking, dynamic programming
Sorting: Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, Merge Sort, Quicksort, lower bounds
Trees: Binary trees, traversing, advanced types of trees, decision trees
Maps and Hash Tables: Key-value stores, hashing, collision resolution
Selected algorithms: Fast matrix multiplication, String matching, Prime numbers
Quantum computing: Qubits, quantum gates, quantum computers, quantum algorithms
teaching_methods: Discussion of scientific articles and current news
assessment_rules: The module examination has a duration of 90 minutes. The weighting of the grade is 5/210.
bibliography: M. Goodrich et al., "Data Structures and Algorithms in Python", John Wiley & Sons, 2013.
R. Sedgewick, "Algorithms", Addison Wesley, fourth edition, 2011.
M. Sipser, "Introduction to the Theory of Computation", Cengage Learning, third edition, 2012.
